svg.title: A journey with room to spare

text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/04/08 - 01 - Essay
Travelers look at a map to consider their route.
Pexels · 12585781
A journey with room to spare
There is more than one way to plan a short trip. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to others are
two useful starting points.
One reason is that checking the route reduces avoidable confusion. For instance, we write down the platform and the
time of the last train. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves us more time to
notice what is happening.
Another reason is that leaving spare time makes changes easier to manage. For example, we choose an earlier bus
rather than risk missing our connection. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than one
person and that different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail.
We can make a sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
Review without reading the example first. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two
reasons are that checking the route reduces avoidable confusion and that leaving spare time makes changes easier to
manage. One example is that we write down the platform and the time of the last train.)
